editorial:
If you love the Ice Age crew, this little TV movie is a fun, cozy watch that feels like a warm hug from old friends. Sid the sloth decides to start an egg-sitting service after a stressed-out bird mom trusts him with her soon-to-hatch egg. Word spreads fast, and soon the whole neighborhood is dropping off eggs. But things go sideways when Squint, a grumpy pirate bunny with a grudge against the herd, steals every single egg and hides them all over the place. It's silly, sweet, and packed with the kind of goofy humor kids adore, while still giving adults a few chuckles along the way.

The animation is bright and colorful, and the voice cast brings their usual charm, especially Sid's clumsy energy. The pacing moves quickly, so little ones won't get bored, though the story is pretty simple and predictable. On the downside, it feels more like a TV special than a full movie, and some jokes land better than others. Still, if you want a light, family-friendly adventure, you should definitely give it a try. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your collection.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Manny, Diego, Sid, and the rest of the herd track down Squint's hidden eggs with help from his twin brother, who switches sides. They find all the eggs scattered across the icy landscape and return them just in time for hatching. Squint's plan falls apart, and the bird families are reunited with their babies. The movie ends on a happy, cheerful note with the herd celebrating together, proving that teamwork and friendship always win the day.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves animated family adventures and the Ice Age characters.
